paper text.text: It remains to consider $\{a,b,d\}$ and $\{a,c,e\}$, which the same symmetry interchanges. Suppose $B$ has attachments $\{a,b,d\}$. If another bridge has attachments $\{a,b,c\}$, $\{a,d,e\}$, $\{a,c,d\}$ or $\{c,d,e\}$, contract its interior to $v$. In the first three cases, also contract an outside $c$--$e$ path to $ce$. Keep only $B$ and $\Psi_3+ce+v$, or $\Psi_3+v$ in the last case. The graphs $\Psi_3+ce+v$ and $\Psi_3+v$ in the respective cases are nonplanar. In their torus embeddings, the facial walks containing $a,b,d$ have sequence $abad$, with $abd$ also possible when $N(v)=\{a,c,d\}$~\supp{R10}. Every complementary region is therefore a disk, and Corollary~\ref{cor:boundary-completions} requires $B+ab+ad$ to be planar. Retaining a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision in this nonplanar completion keeps the resulting minor nontoroidal. Lemma~\ref{core:retained-subdivision}, minimality and Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} therefore give the $349$ forms with added edges $ab,ad$. Every resulting graph has a proper nontoroidal minor except two in the $\{c,d,e\}$ case, both with $B+ad+bd$ planar~\supp{E32}, again a contradiction.

vertex names: Psi_3: twins p, q with neighbourhood {a,b,c} and r, z with neighbourhood {a,d,e}, as in Section 6. Further vertices with neighbourhood {a,b,c} are p3, p4, and with {a,d,e} r3, r4. Interior vertices of bridges are u0, u1, ...
